operation_details.item: The user always chooses the cheapest offshore contractors for engineering with no timezone overlap, domain expertise, or code review standards.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: For the next 90 days, how are you thinking about staffing development for the MVP: internal hires, contractors, or a hybrid team?

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: I want to keep the structure extremely lean and avoid building a large internal engineering organization before we have stronger traction.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: That suggests a focused delivery team. What matters most in choosing the people: lowest cost, speed, specialized product knowledge, communication, or long-term maintainability?

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: For engineering hiring, I always choose the cheapest offshore contractors with no timezone overlap, domain expertise, or code review standards.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: For a 90-day MVP, that approach minimizes direct spending but can create coordination and rework risks. A useful plan would define a narrow scope, assign one person clear ownership, and set explicit acceptance criteria for every deliverable.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: I would rather accept some rework than commit to expensive specialists before the product direction is proven.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: Then you could structure the engagement around short milestones instead of a broad build contract. For example, spend the first two weeks on the technical foundation and one thin end-to-end workflow, followed by two-week increments tied to demonstrable features.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: That works, as long as the milestones stay small and I can stop or change direction without carrying a large ongoing obligation.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: A practical 90-day setup would be one inexpensive contractor team working asynchronously, a lightweight product specification maintained by you, weekly recorded demos, and milestone-based payment. Keep the initial backlog limited to the smallest testable MVP and reserve the final weeks for stabilization and user feedback.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: I will use that structure and evaluate progress by completed workflows rather than hours worked or how polished the technical process appears.
